newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon confirms plane parts are from A-10.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon confirms plane parts are from A-10.

text.p: Two small pieces of metal recovered from a snowy peak in the Rocky Mountains have been identified as parts of the wreckage of an A-10 warplane loaded with bombs that disappeared three weeks ago, a senior Air Force official said Wednesday.
"They have identified the parts as part of Capt. Button's airplane," the official said. "They checked the serial numbers of the parts and they are from Capt. Button's aircraft."

An Air Force helicopter crewman recovered the two pieces of metal earlier Wednesday from the site where the wreckage was believed to be buried. The official said the Air Force would attempt to move more personnel to the area Thursday in an attempt to locate Capt. Craig Button, 32, who inexplicably left the three-plane delta formation in which he was flying and apparently veered northeast into Colorado, some 850 miles (1,350 km) away from an April 2 training exercise.
The A-10 Thunderbolt attack bomber was thought to have slammed into the side of the 12,500-foot (3,800-metre) -high New York Mountain in the remote Sawatch range southeast of the Vail ski resort.
The wreckage was spotted on Sunday by an Army National Guard helicopter crew near a steep cliff on New York Mountain.
